findings.rule: 271-c15 / D40 (labels never clipped) and process rule 'no weakened tests'; the PR body states 'No assertion was loosened'
findings.trigger: The red commit asserted !layout.hasVisualOverflow (width OR height). The impl commit replaced it with didOverflowHeight plus layout.size <= node.size. TextLayoutResult.size is coerced to the incoming constraints, so the size check cannot see horizontal overflow. A softWrap=false chrome label wider than its slot (for example a top-bar action or tab label at font 2.0 / 337dp) is clipped and the test still passes. Horizontal overflow is the D40 failure mode #307 hit.
findings.title: Screenshot no-truncation check dropped the width-overflow assertion in the impl commit
findings.proof: Add assertFalse("$text overflows its width", layout.didOverflowWidth) back to assertNoTruncatedText and run :app:testDemoDebugUnitTest --tests '*ShellChromeScreenshotTest*'. Either it passes (restore the assertion) or it names the text that is clipped at 2.0/337dp (a real D40 defect that the relaxation hid).

findings.rule: 271-c3 (issue AC1: walk asserts the T-table chrome on each screen of the real flow)
findings.trigger: The walk does shell.show(SignIn) and then navigate(Upload), so Upload has an entry below and is asserted with Back. The prototype signIn() does root('upload'), so in the real flow Upload has an empty stack and T gives no back. The walk therefore approves a stack that the prototype never produces. It would stay green if sign-in completion left SignIn under Upload, letting back return to Sign in.
findings.title: Walk test pushes Upload over SignIn instead of rooting it, so it asserts Back on Upload
findings.proof: Change the walk to shell.root(UploadNavKey()) after SignIn (matching the prototype's root on sign-in) and assert rowOf(Upload) with leading = None via assertChrome(row, leading = None).

findings.rule: Prototype logic go/swap/back/root (Prototype.dc.html l.1039-1042), which all set sheet: null; 271-c11 one shared sheet host
findings.trigger: A W4 screen shows a sheet through LocalTmrSheetHost (status sheet on appDetail, delete-account sheet on settings) and the stack then changes without dismiss(): a sheet action that calls root(SignIn), a tab or Close tap, or a fallback goBack. TmrSheetHostState.current survives, so the old sheet, with content captured from the previous entry, stays drawn over the new screen. The shell is the one owner of the host and the stack, so it should clear the sheet once there rather than in every W4 caller.
findings.title: Shell sheet host is not dismissed when the current NavKey changes
findings.proof: ShellHostsTest: show a sheet from the EditResume entry, call shell.navigator.goBack(), and assert onAllNodesWithTag(SHEET_TAG).assertCountEquals(0). It fails at head. LaunchedEffect(key) { sheetHost.dismiss() } in TmrShell fixes it.
